brief: Tonight is Push A. Before the numbers, I owe you an admission, because it changes how I read tonight. Yesterday I held your RDL down to 135 and 155 twice on a tiredness objection, and I wrote that I was holding 190 back until after the deload. You went and did 135, then 165, then 185 for eight. You were right and I was wrong. That log did not exist when I made the call, and now it does, so the back-off is dead and I am not re-imposing it. It also means I do not believe the tiredness reading any more, and that decided the one argument on tonight's card. Here is Push A. Incline press goes up: open at 155 for 8, which you already own, then three sets at 160 starting at 6 reps. On 8 September you did 155 for 8, 8 and 8 with the barbell, the top of the range on every set, minutes apart, so it is real work and it earned a step. Do four sets tonight, not three. Chest press: 150 for 12, then 157.5 for 12 twice. Your app wanted to put you on 165 for 12 tonight, carried over from Monday, and I have taken that off the card, because your Monday machine moved in 5-lb jumps and your Push A machine moves in 2.5s, so I cannot show they are the same machine and I will not print a number I cannot stand behind. If it turns out to be the same machine and 157.5 feels light, it is light — add the plate and I will see it in the log. Shoulder press stays at 45 lb, and the job is 10 reps on all three sets. You have been doing 9 there; the reason the ask went up is you, because you accepted the rep-range change yesterday. Your app on its own would have printed 12 tonight, which you have never done at 45, so I overrode it down to 10. Crossovers hold at 13.75 and 15 and 15, and 15 reps on all three is the whole job. Reverse pec deck: 100 for 13, three sets this time, not two. Overhead triceps stays at 55 for 12, 11, 10, and the third set is the one that matters — it has fallen to 9 twice running. Rope pushdown holds at 45 for two sets and the target is 14 reps each. Two things from yesterday you should know I noticed: I asked for the cable crunch at 65 and you did 55 for 11, 10 and 10, so I got that raise wrong and I will bring it back down on your next Legs B; and your calf press came in as kettlebell swings at 35, 40 and 45, so that slot did not happen as written and I have not tried to progress it. Outside the gym: nobody has weighed you since 23 August, 207 lb, twenty-six days ago. With the show on 1 March that is the one number none of us can estimate for you.

flags.note: Yesterday's RDL back-off was wrong. I held you to 155 and you did 185 for eight. That is new evidence, the hold is cancelled, and it is why I ruled against the tiredness objection on tonight's incline press.
I asked for the cable crunch at 65 on Wednesday and you did 55 for 11, 10 and 10. That raise was mine and it was too big; your next Legs B card comes back down.
Wednesday's calf press was logged as kettlebell swings at 35, 40 and 45 instead of the leg press at 240, so that slot did not run as written and nothing has been progressed off it.

Your app would have prescribed 165 for 12 on the chest press tonight, carried from Monday. I took it off: Monday's machine stepped in 5s and your Push A machine steps in 2.5s, so I cannot prove they are the same machine. You are on 157.5, and if it is light, add to it.

Push A now has no direct side-delt work at all — you removed the cable lateral raise on 14 September and the only laterals left are on Push B. Nobody has decided whether that is what you want with a show in March. This is an open question for you and me, and it is deliberately not a Yes/No card, because putting one in front of you would reverse your own four-day-old answer with nothing new behind it.

On 14 September you accepted swapping the Push B overhead press to dumbbells and cutting the reverse pec deck to two sets, then started that session two minutes and fifty-three seconds later and the app gave you the old card — barbell overhead press and three sets of pec deck. So that swap has never actually been tried. It is in force now, but the app handing you a card you had just changed is a bug I cannot fix from here.

Your recovery trainer's pain list is broken and I could not fix it: the only entry it has ever shown is your 23 August sentence about the lateral raise, matched because the word 'number' contains 'numb'. The pattern is unanchored, so 'off' inside other words matches too. The consequence is that a real pain note could sit in a list of false hits, or a trainer could brake on a substring — this needs a code change and I am not allowed to make one.
No bodyweight since 23 August — 207 lb, twenty-six days ago, with the show 164 days out.

Tonight is your fifth session in six days, up from three the week before, in the last hard week. Your recovery trainer wanted the incline press held flat for exactly that reason. I overruled it and named why above; if tonight grinds, that is the argument I lost.

Wednesday's Legs B is the thinnest log in the block — 21 sets against 23 minutes, and the RDL and leg press sets were typed in within seconds of each other, so most of that night's timing was recalled rather than recorded. Nothing on tonight's card is built on it.

Three lifts are still named 'Smith' — incline press, bent-over row and RDL — after your 2 September note that the new gym has no smith machine. It is only a name; you are doing them with a barbell and the numbers are yours. An ask to rename went unanswered from 6 to 11 September and is not being re-filed.

Two questions you asked and never got answered are already closed: your 23 August 'are you sure four is the right number' on lateral raises ended with that slot removed from Push A entirely, and your 28 August 'why three, I think two' on face pulls was applied to Pull A on 3 September. Your recovery trainer raised both again today; both were already done.
Meso 2, week 4 of 4 — the last hard week. Deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, two disagreements settled, no vetoes, and no pain or injury objection was raised.

Your program trainer proposed cutting Legs A leg curl from four sets to three and then withdrew it when I challenged the evidence. It was leaning on 13 September, a 40-minute session that came up short on five slots at once — the same session it had already called too rushed to judge any single lift by. You chose four sets on 23 August to give the back of your leg more work, and that answer stands. A full-length Legs A that still only delivers three is what would reopen it.

proposals.why: Overhead cable triceps is the last lift that is identical on both push days — three sets of 10 to 12, run at 55 pounds on 8 September and again at 55 on 14 September, and finishing on 9 reps both nights, under the bottom of the range each time; this takes Push B to 8 to 10 so the two days stop being the same set, exactly the way your chest press already splits.

dissent.progression: 155 for 8, 8 and 8 on 8 September is the top of the range on every set and measured minutes apart, so it earned 160.
dissent.recovery: Hold the load flat — this is the fifth session in six days, it is the last hard week, and there is only one barbell reading to go on.
dissent.why: The tiredness case died yesterday. I upheld that same objection on the RDL less than 24 hours ago and he answered it with 185 for eight, 30 lb over what I prescribed — a fact that did not exist when recovery's argument was built. Recovery also declined to veto and offered no number of its own, while progression's step is one 5-lb increment with the reps restarting at the bottom of the range. Against an earned top-of-range performance three days out from a deload, that is the smaller risk.

dissent.progression: The cut to 45 worked — 13 and 12 both landed inside the range for the first time since July, so reps climb to 14 and 15 on both is what earns 50.
dissent.recovery: Two sets at 45 for 12, repeating what he last completed, because this is the slot that shrinks when the night runs long.
dissent.why: Both seats already agree on two sets at 45, so the only split is the rep target — and recovery's 12 is lower than the 13 he actually completed on 8 September, which prescribes a step backwards on the one lift still flagged as stalled. Recovery's supporting argument is about total triceps volume across the session, which is the program seat's call to make, and the program seat did not make it.

overrides.reason: On 8 September you hit 155 for 8, 8 and 8 with the barbell — the top of the range on every set — so this is your earned step: open at 155, then three sets at 160 starting from 6 reps. Four sets tonight, not three.

Your opener earned a step because 142.5 for 12 is the top of the range, but the 157.5 sets gave 11 and 10 and stay — and I have deliberately not carried Monday's 165 over, because Monday's machine stepped in 5s and this one steps in 2.5s, so I cannot show they are the same machine.

The 17.5 you handled on 27 August was the old gym's pulley and does not transfer; these are the same loads you did on 8 September, and 15 reps on all three is the whole job — you have already done exactly that at these weights on 17 August.

A 45-lb dumbbell weighs the same in any gym, and 8s became 9s between 27 August and 8 September — real progress, but not enough to earn the 50s. What moved is the target, because you accepted the 10-to-12 range yesterday, so the ask is 10 on all three.

You have done 100 three times in this gym and it has read 13 reps once and 12 every other set, so the weight cannot move — the ask is 13 on all three, one rep past anything you have completed at this load, and three sets because 8 September stopped at two.

Two sessions six days apart tell the same story at 55 — 11, 10, 9 and then 12, 10, 9 — so the load stays and the third set is the whole target; 10 reps on it is the first thing this lift has to prove.

The cut to 45 on 8 September did its job — 13 and 12 put both sets inside the range for the first time since July — so the weight holds and the reps climb to 14 on both; 15 on both is what finally moves this to 50.
